newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Police remand Hebron gunman, hold second suspect.
newsitem.headline: Police remand Hebron gunman, hold second suspect.

text.p: Israeli police have arrested a second man in connection with Wednesday's shooting of seven Palestinians in the West Bank town of Hebron by an off-duty soldier, security sources said on Thursday.
An Israeli court remanded Noam Friedman, suspected of opening fire on Palestinians in a crowded outdoor market in Hebron, in custody for 10 days.
The sources identified the second suspect as Yuval Jibli, 21, a soldier serving in the same army unit with Friedman. They did not say when he was arrested.
Israel Radio and the domestic Itim news service said Jibli was suspected of helping Friedman plan the attack and would be brought before a judge later on Thursday.
Itim said police had asked the judge to hold Friedman, 22, for 15 days but the court extended the remand by only 10 days.
Friedman, an Orthodox Jew from the Maaleh Adumim settlement in the West Bank, is suspected of attempted murder and sedition.
He told investigators he wanted to sabotage any transfer of power to Palestinians in Hebron under an agreement Israel and the PLO were set to sign.
